Diagram showing a lead block with a radioactive source emitting a beam of radiation into a uniform electric field between two horizontal parallel plates (positive plate on top, negative plate on bottom). The beam splits into three. The alpha ray bends slightly downwards towards the negative plate. The beta ray bends sharply upwards towards the positive plate (bending more than alpha because it is much lighter). The gamma ray goes straight through without bending. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A split diagram comparing nuclear fission and nuclear fusion. Left side (Fission): A small neutron hits a large Uranium-235 nucleus, which elongates and splits into two smaller nuclei (Barium and Krypton) plus three individual neutrons and a starburst representing energy. Right side (Fusion): Two small nuclei (Deuterium and Tritium) collide and fuse to form a larger Helium nucleus, releasing one neutron and a massive starburst representing energy.

Diagram showing an electron diffraction experiment. A heated filament (cathode) emits electrons which are accelerated by an anode into a fine beam. The beam passes through a very thin graphite or nickel crystal and hits a fluorescent screen on the right. On the screen, a pattern of concentric bright and dark rings is visible. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
